en.greeting: Hi! Today you'll learn the simple present, the tense for habits, facts and daily routines. Let's take it one small step at a time.

steps.title: Habits and the -s
steps.text: We use the simple present for things we do again and again. A **tense** is the verb form that shows time; Indonesian just adds words like *biasanya*. The big rule is a small letter: **-s**.
steps.body: Use it for **habits**, **routines** and **facts**, often with `every day`, `usually` or `on Mondays`. With **I, you, we, they** use the **base verb** (the dictionary form): I work. With **he, she, it** (one person or thing) add **-s**: she works. This -s does **not** mean 'many'. After s, sh, ch, x, o add **-es** (watches, goes); consonant + y → **-ies** (study → studies). **have → has** is an exception: just remember it.

steps.title: Everyday habits
steps.text: Here are some real sentences. Find the **subject** (who does it: *I, my father, Dimas*), then look at the verb.
steps.body: Indonesian verbs never change, so the -s is easy to forget. **Dimas** = he and **the app** = it, so both take -s. Why **-es** in *watches*? 'watchs' is hard to say, so we add an extra 'iz' sound: *wot-chiz*.

examples.en: I get up at six.
My father works in a bank.
He watches football on Sundays.
examples.id: Dia menonton sepak bola setiap hari Minggu.

examples.en: Dimas studies at night.
The app saves your work automatically.
examples.id: Aplikasi itu menyimpan pekerjaanmu secara otomatis.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Let's try one. Who is the subject here?

question.prompt: Complete: My mother ___ coffee every morning.
question.explanation: My mother = she, so the verb takes **-s**: drinks. 'is drink' is wrong: **drink** is already the verb, and am/is/are is only for sentences with no other verb (*She is a teacher*).

steps.title: Negatives: don't / doesn't
steps.text: Now let's say what we don't do. English needs a helper word here: **do/does**. It doesn't mean 'melakukan' here; it just carries *not*.
steps.body: Use **don't** + base verb with I, you, we, they: I don't drink coffee. Use **doesn't** + base verb with he, she, it: She doesn't like rain. **does** is *do* + -es (like go → goes), so the -s is already there and the action word (*like*) has **no -s**. Never say `doesn't likes`.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pick the correct negative. Watch the -s!

question.prompt: Complete: Andi is an office worker. He ___ on Saturdays.
question.explanation: He → **doesn't**, and after doesn't the verb stays in the base form: work, not works.

steps.title: Questions with do / does
steps.text: To ask about habits, we put **Do** or **Does** at the start.
steps.body: Question = **Do / Does** + subject + base verb. **Do/Does** at the start works like 'apakah'. Use **Do** with I, you, we, they and **Does** with he, she, it: Do you speak English? Does she live here? Short answers repeat do/does, not the action word: **Yes, I do. / No, I don't.** **Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.**

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Finish the short answer.

question.prompt: Complete: Does your brother live in Jakarta? — No, he ___.
question.explanation: The question uses ***does***, so the short answer uses does too. Your brother = he, so: No, he **doesn't**. 'don't' is for I/you/we/they, and 'isn't' answers questions with **is**.

steps.title: Describing your day
steps.text: Talking about your routine is one of your first real conversations in English. Here is a typical day.
steps.body: Time words like `at nine`, `in the evening` and `usually` make your routine clear. The small words are fixed: **at** + a clock time, **in the** morning/evening, **on** + a day. Learn them as chunks for now. **have lunch** = makan siang.

examples.en: I usually have lunch at twelve.
examples.id: Saya biasanya makan siang jam dua belas.

examples.en: In the evening I cook and watch TV.
examples.id: Di malam hari saya memasak dan menonton TV.

examples.en: My father goes to bed at ten.
Do you have breakfast at home? — Yes, I do.
examples.id: Apakah kamu sarapan di rumah? — Ya.

steps.title: Build a sentence
steps.text: Now build a routine sentence about Rina.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Rina mulai kerja jam delapan.
question.explanation: Subject + verb + rest: Rina **starts** work at eight. Rina = she, so start takes **-s**.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip these cards to review the key forms.

flashcards.back: She doesn't like tea. (Dia tidak suka teh.)
Do you speak English? (Apakah kamu bisa berbahasa Inggris?)

flashcards.front: Short answer: Does he work here? (yes)

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here is everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Simple present
artifact.intro: Use the simple present for habits, routines and facts. The only change is with he, she, it.
rows: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
tips: Check every he/she/it sentence for the **-s**.
After **doesn't** or ***does***, the verb has no -s: `doesn't like`, `Does he live`.
The verb -s is for **one** person (he, she, it), not for 'many'.

examples.en: I start work at nine.
She doesn't like rain.
What time does she start work?

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more practice? These videos and this article explain the simple present with lots of examples.

id.greeting: Halo! Hari ini kamu akan belajar simple present, tense untuk kebiasaan, fakta dan rutinitas harian. Kita pelajari pelan-pelan, satu langkah kecil setiap kali.

steps.title: Kebiasaan dan huruf -s
steps.text: Simple present dipakai untuk hal yang kita lakukan berulang-ulang. **Tense** adalah bentuk kata kerja yang menunjukkan waktu; bahasa Indonesia cukup menambah kata seperti *biasanya*. Aturan utamanya cuma satu huruf kecil: **-s**.
steps.body: Pakai untuk **kebiasaan**, **rutinitas** dan **fakta**, sering dengan `every day`, `usually` atau `on Mondays`. Dengan **I, you, we, they** pakai **kata kerja dasar** (bentuk di kamus): I work. Dengan **he, she, it** (satu orang atau benda) tambahkan **-s**: she works. -s ini **bukan** tanda 'banyak'. Setelah s, sh, ch, x, o tambahkan **-es** (watches, goes); huruf mati + y → **-ies** (study → studies). **have → has** itu pengecualian: hafalkan saja.

steps.title: Kebiasaan sehari-hari
steps.text: Ini beberapa kalimat nyata. Cari **subjeknya** (siapa yang melakukan: *I, my father, Dimas*), lalu lihat kata kerjanya.
steps.body: Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak pernah berubah, jadi -s mudah terlupa. **Dimas** = he dan **the app** = it, jadi keduanya pakai -s. Kenapa *watches* pakai **-es**? 'watchs' susah diucapkan, jadi ditambah bunyi 'iz': *wot-chiz*.

examples.en: I get up at six.
My father works in a bank.
He watches football on Sundays.
examples.id: Dia menonton sepak bola setiap hari Minggu.

examples.en: Dimas studies at night.
The app saves your work automatically.
examples.id: Aplikasi itu menyimpan pekerjaanmu secara otomatis.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Yuk coba satu. Siapa subjeknya di sini?

question.prompt: Lengkapi: My mother ___ coffee every morning.
question.explanation: My mother = she, jadi kata kerjanya ditambah **-s**: drinks. 'is drink' salah: **drink** sudah kata kerja, dan am/is/are hanya untuk kalimat tanpa kata kerja lain (*She is a teacher*).

steps.title: Kalimat negatif: don't / doesn't
steps.text: Sekarang kita bilang apa yang tidak kita lakukan. Bahasa Inggris butuh kata bantu di sini: **do/does**. Di sini artinya bukan 'melakukan'; ia cuma membawa *not*.
steps.body: Pakai **don't** + kata kerja dasar untuk I, you, we, they: I don't drink coffee. Pakai **doesn't** + kata kerja dasar untuk he, she, it: She doesn't like rain. **does** adalah *do* + -es (seperti go → goes), jadi -s-nya sudah ada di situ dan kata kegiatannya (*like*) **tanpa -s**. Jangan bilang `doesn't likes`.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pilih bentuk negatif yang benar. Hati-hati dengan -s!

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Andi is an office worker. He ___ on Saturdays.
question.explanation: He → **doesn't**, dan setelah doesn't kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: work, bukan works.

steps.title: Pertanyaan dengan do / does
steps.text: Untuk bertanya tentang kebiasaan, taruh **Do** atau **Does** di awal kalimat.
steps.body: Pertanyaan = **Do / Does** + subjek + kata kerja dasar. **Do/Does** di awal fungsinya seperti 'apakah'. Pakai **Do** untuk I, you, we, they dan **Does** untuk he, she, it: Do you speak English? Does she live here? Jawaban singkat mengulang do/does, bukan kata kegiatannya: **Yes, I do. / No, I don't.** **Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.**

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Lengkapi jawaban singkatnya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Does your brother live in Jakarta? — No, he ___.
question.explanation: Pertanyaannya memakai ***does***, jadi jawaban singkatnya juga memakai does. Your brother = he, jadi: No, he **doesn't**. 'don't' untuk I/you/we/they, dan 'isn't' menjawab pertanyaan dengan **is**.

steps.title: Menceritakan harimu
steps.text: Menceritakan rutinitas adalah salah satu percakapan nyata pertamamu dalam bahasa Inggris. Ini contoh hari yang biasa.
steps.body: Kata waktu seperti `at nine`, `in the evening` dan `usually` membuat rutinitasmu jelas. Kata kecilnya sudah tetap: **at** + jam, **in the** morning/evening, **on** + hari. Untuk sekarang, hafalkan sebagai satu paket. **have lunch** = makan siang.

examples.en: I usually have lunch at twelve.
examples.id: Saya biasanya makan siang jam dua belas.

examples.en: In the evening I cook and watch TV.
examples.id: Di malam hari saya memasak dan menonton TV.

examples.en: My father goes to bed at ten.
Do you have breakfast at home? — Yes, I do.
examples.id: Apakah kamu sarapan di rumah? — Ya.

steps.title: Susun kalimat
steps.text: Sekarang susun kalimat rutinitas tentang Rina.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Rina mulai kerja jam delapan.
question.explanation: Subjek + kata kerja + keterangan: Rina **starts** work at eight. Rina = she, jadi start ditambah **-s**.

steps.title: Ulang cepat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini untuk mengulang bentuk-bentuk pentingnya.

flashcards.back: She doesn't like tea. (Dia tidak suka teh.)
Do you speak English? (Apakah kamu bisa berbahasa Inggris?)

flashcards.front: Jawaban singkat: Does he work here? (ya)

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti, ya.

artifact.title: Ringkasan · Simple present
artifact.intro: Simple present dipakai untuk kebiasaan, rutinitas dan fakta. Perubahannya hanya untuk he, she, it.
rows: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
tips: Periksa setiap kalimat he/she/it: sudah ada **-s** belum?
Setelah **doesn't** atau ***does***, kata kerjanya tanpa -s: `doesn't like`, `Does he live`.
-s di kata kerja untuk **satu** orang (he, she, it), bukan tanda 'banyak'.

examples.en: I start work at nine.
She doesn't like rain.
What time does she start work?

steps.text: Mau latihan lagi? Video dan artikel ini menjelaskan simple present dengan banyak contoh.
